quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce on XYWAV durability: 'We have not really seen any material impacts from those generics coming into the market,' and '80% or more patients with narcolepsy and IH have comorbidities, cardiovascular and cardiometabolic comorbidities,' which keeps the low-sodium option important. Orexins will enter in the NT1 indication, 'which is less than half of the overall narcolepsy space'; from what Jazz understands, healthcare providers will not switch the stable base of XYWAV patients away, though 'it takes longer for patients to get to Xywav if they are trying the orexin first,' and 'we do not see this business being dramatically disrupted.' On idiopathic hypersomnia she cited estimates of a prevalent population 'maybe similar to narcolepsy, maybe 100,000 patients', diagnosed patients 'around about 37,000' and treated patients 'maybe 9,000', leaving significant room for XYWAV to grow.
quarterly_data.figure: 80% or more of narcolepsy and IH patients have comorbidities; IH prevalent maybe 100,000, diagnosed around about 37,000, treated maybe 9,000

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce: Epidiolex delivered '$292 million, 16% revenue growth, 14% volume growth' in the second quarter. Much of the growth comes from the adult segment, which is more fragmented than the pediatric segment and still has significant headroom, and Jazz is investing in JazzCares support to keep patients on treatment longer. Because Epidiolex is weight-based, adults can take a large volume of the sesame-oil-based oral solution, which can limit adult uptake; Jazz expects the capsule formulation (NDA submitted) to expand the overall patient pool. She said the ANDA settlements out to the late 2030s opened the opportunity to invest in a phase III DEE study, a phase II/III study in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, an adult LGS study and an earlier focal-onset seizure study.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 Epidiolex $292 million, 16% revenue growth, 14% volume growth

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce on the Ziihera peak-revenue raise: 'A few years ago, when we initially looked at the potential for Ziihera, we did talk about it being a $2 billion-plus opportunity', covering BTC, first-line GEA, metastatic breast cancer and pan-tumor; the raised $3 billion-$5 billion range now also includes colorectal cancer, non-small cell lung cancer and early breast cancer. For the first-line GEA launch she said Jazz is 'not anticipating a lot of payer friction' given the permanent J-code, expects patient access from the beginning and needs a quick start in community as well as academic centers. Head of IR John Bluth said the pan-tumor trial is 'enrolling nicely' with no readout timing provided, and the doublet overall-survival data will be shown at a future medical meeting not yet named.
quarterly_data.figure: prior Ziihera peak view $2 billion-plus; raised to $3 billion-$5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce: Modeyso launched last August and 'we are already annualizing at $200 million with more than 600 patients having been treated', which reinforces Jazz's belief in the $500 million U.S. peak sales opportunity (including first line). Second-line use is still growing, with room to improve testing rates and the timeliness of referrals to academic centers of excellence. The ACTION study (readout in the first half of 2027) would let patients receive Modeyso immediately after radiotherapy instead of waiting for progression, which she expects to make more patients eligible and improve duration of treatment - an inflection she called important to reach the $500 million peak.
quarterly_data.figure: Modeyso annualizing at $200 million; $500 million U.S. peak sales opportunity

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce on Zepzelca: since the first-line maintenance launch Jazz's focus has been '100% commercially on first-line', which generated around 30%-40% of second-quarter revenue; the second-line business is expected to taper away, and she expects the first-line segment to 'become a little bit more competitive with the entrance of new competitors', while Zepzelca is particularly appreciated in the community setting because it is easier to use without the monitoring.
quarterly_data.figure: around 30%-40% of Q2 Zepzelca revenue from first-line maintenance

quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR John Bluth on business development: the focus is rare disease where Jazz has competency in epilepsy, sleep and oncology, citing over the past 12 to 18 months the Chimerix acquisition (Modeyso), the Saniona acquisition of early epilepsy opportunities, the AbCellera deal in oncology and, most recently, Actio Biosciences in epilepsy. Outside its core areas Jazz is 'less likely to go very early' and more likely to look at proof of concept or later; inside them it is open to earlier transactions and closer-to-commercial deals - 'Look for more from us going forward.' CCO Sam Pearce expects 'very significant commercial synergies' from Actio's KCNT1 epilepsy asset, which shares the core call point with pediatric epileptologists that Epidiolex has; additional commercial investments have not been detailed, and after closing the Jazz team will drive the program forward.
